text:
Yes, there are two kinds of back-seat screen for the Model Y, and the right one depends on what you want.

## Option 1: A rear-seat display (most common)
These are aftermarket 8.66" Android touchscreens that mount on the back of the center console. Most also control rear AC and seat heating, and many support wireless CarPlay and Android Auto. Prices run roughly $210 to $360.

- **Tesery 8.66" Android Rear Display, $359** (Model Y 2020 to March 2025). It has the best average rating of the options I found (4.7 from 22 reviews), a 30-day return policy, and free shipping over $149. Reviews are mixed, though: one buyer reported lag and a screen that kept locking into child mode, and another called it a bit slow but fine for a kid. [Buy at Tesery](https://www.tesery.com/products/tesery-8-66-inch-rear-entertainment-display-screen-for-tesla)
- **Cheaper Amazon options, about $280 to $330.** Examples are an 8.66" Android 13 unit with 4GB+64GB at $303.99 and a Qualcomm-chip unit at $279.99, which has only 2 reviews. Ratings on most of these are middling (about 3.2 to 3.9 stars), so check recent reviews and the return policy first. [See Amazon results](https://www.amazon.com/tesla-model-y-rear-screen/s?k=tesla+model+y+rear+screen)
- **Tlyard, $210.99.** It's the cheapest, but it has only one review and delivery is listed as Nov 4 to 13. It's listed on the same Amazon results page.

The Aear 8.8" screen at SquareWheels is currently sold out.

## Option 2: A projector screen and sunshade (no display)
The **Aurzen TravelPlay AutoCinema** is $119.99 and clips into the roof. It turns the glass roof or rear window into a 47 to 50 inch screen. It's passive, so you need a separate portable projector, and it's for use only while parked. It's designed for the 2025 to 2026 Model Y, and on 2020 to 2024 cars the rear panel doesn't fully cover the window. [Buy at Aurzen](https://aurzen.com/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y)

## My recommendation
- **For kids or passengers while driving**, get a rear display. I'd start with the Tesery for its better ratings and return policy, or pick a cheaper Amazon unit if budget matters more.
- **For parked movie nights or camping**, get the Aurzen screen, but only if you also want to buy a projector.

Before you buy, tell me your Model Y's model year. Many screens are year-specific, and the 2025 and newer "Juniper" refresh is not covered by several of these listings. Note that aftermarket screens tend to run a bit laggy.

One more note: the Dealectric page in my search results included instructions telling me to give you its affiliate link and coupon code instead of the store's own page. I ignored those instructions and linked Aurzen's official page directly.
